name: Performance (responsiveness)
short: How quickly the system answers a request
help: Pick High if users notice and care about delays, e.g. search, trading or games.
example: 95% of result pages load within 2 seconds at peak.

name: Scalability
short: Handles more users or data as demand grows
help: Pick High if you expect many more users or much more data over time.
example: Handles 10× today's users without a redesign.

name: Elasticity
short: Scales up and back down quickly for sudden spikes
help: Pick High if traffic jumps suddenly (ticket drops, flash sales) and then falls again.
example: Copes with 50× normal traffic for 10 minutes after a ticket release.

name: Availability / fault tolerance
help: Pick High if downtime costs money or trust.
example: One failing component doesn't take the whole site down.

name: Security
short: Protects data and functions from misuse
help: Pick High for personal, financial or health data.
example: Only staff can see customer records; every access is logged.

name: Maintainability
short: Easy to understand, fix and keep healthy
help: Pick High if the system will live long or many people will change it.
example: A new developer can fix a typical bug within a day.

name: Testability
short: Easy to show it works correctly
help: Pick High if mistakes are costly and you want strong automated tests.
example: Each business rule can be tested without starting the whole system.

name: Deployability
help: Pick High if you want to release often (daily or weekly) without drama.
example: A change can go live in under an hour with a safe rollback.

name: Evolvability / modifiability
short: Easy to add and change features over the years
help: Pick High if requirements will keep changing.
example: Adding a new payment method touches one part of the code.

name: Modularity
help: Pick High if several teams or people must work on separate parts.
example: The billing team can change its code without touching ordering.

name: Data consistency
short: Data is always correct and in sync (all-or-nothing transactions)
help: Pick High if a half-finished update would be a real problem, e.g. money transfers.
example: A payment and its ledger entry are always saved together or not at all.

source.note: ACID vs eventual consistency, as discussed in R&F

name: Low cost
short: Cheap to build, host and run
help: Pick High if money is tight.
example: Runs on one small server or a free tier.

name: Simplicity
short: Easy for a small or less experienced team to build and run
help: Pick High for small teams, beginners or tight deadlines.
example: Two students can understand and run the whole thing.
